title: The morphism into projective space over S given by an invertible module and generating sections
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $n\ge0$, and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ the projective space over $S$ of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with structure morphism $q_n=\mathrm{pr}_1:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ and second projection $\mathrm{pr}_2:\mathbf P^n_S\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$. Let $Y$ be a scheme with a morphism $g:Y\to S$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ global sections generating $\mathcal L$. Let $\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ be the morphism attached to $(\mathcal L,(s_i))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points]. Define

$$
\varphi_{g,(\mathcal L,(s_0,\dots,s_n))}:Y\longrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S
$$

as the unique morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varphi=g$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\varphi=\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}$, given by the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] (the two composites $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ agree because $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is terminal [lem-weil-pbc-spec-z-terminal]). Thus $\varphi$ is a morphism over $S$ (with $Y$ viewed over $S$ by $g$), "given on coordinates by $(s_0:\dots:s_n)$".

source.place: Constructions, Section 27.13 (Tag 01ND), the paragraph after Definition 27.13.2 (Tag 01NF): 'Given a scheme Y over S and a pair (L,(s_0,...,s_n)) as in Lemma 27.13.1 the induced morphism to P^n_S is denoted phi_(L,(s_0,...,s_n)) ... the pair defines a morphism into P^n_Z and we already have the structure morphism into S so combined we get a morphism into P^n_S = P^n_Z x S'
